notes: No genuine Bestsellers-type PLP found on woodenstreet.com. Access: direct HTTP fetch throughout, no WAF/bot-block, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only legacy scraper-bot blocks e.g. Scrapy/HTTrack/Teleport). Checked: (1) homepage header/mega-menu HTML - only relevant nav label present is 'New Arrivals'; no Best Seller/Bestseller/Top Seller/Popular/Trending/Customer Favorites nav item. (2) categories.xml sitemap (1684 category URLs) - zero matches for best/popular/trend/top-sell keywords. (3) under-categories.xml (58 price-tier URLs like beds-under-20000) - none relevant. (4) Direct URL probes, all 404: /best-sellers, /bestsellers, /best-selling-furniture, /top-selling-furniture, /best-selling, /trending, /trending-products, /popular-products, /top-rated, /customer-favorites, /most-popular. (5) Homepage has a 'Top-Rated by Indian Homes' product carousel, but its own 'View All' CTA resolves to https://www.woodenstreet.com/deal-of-the-day (breadcrumb 'Furniture sale > Deal of the day') - a discount/price-promo page, not a distinct popularity/bestseller-curated listing, so it does not qualify as a Bestsellers PLP under section 3 (page must itself represent the bestseller/popularity concept, not just be linked from a section with a rating-flavored title). (6) Site's own search (/search?q=bestseller, /search?q=best+seller) returns a generic client-rendered 'Search Wooden Street' template with no SSR product_count - matches the known false-absence pattern for this site's search, so treated as inconclusive rather than proof, and not relied upon; navigation + sitemap evidence above is the actual basis for absence. Site is Next.js SSR (site is furniture-led per prior Home-Decor pass); every real listing page embeds __NEXT_DATA__ ...apiResData.data.product_count, and none of the tested best/top/popular URL shapes returned that structure (all 404).
